s: Why R 0 must be an expected-cost measure, and when worst-case and expected cost differ.
x: Two orthogonal choices define a randomized measure: 1. Error model. Zero error / one-sided error / bounded error / unbounded error. ( ZPP / RP / BPP / PP .) 2. Cost model. Worst-case number of queries over all coin flips, or expected number of queries. The zero-error trap If you demand zero error and worst-case cost , you get D (f) exactly: fix the coins of an always-correct depth- T algorithm and you have a deterministic depth- T tree. So R 0 and Q 0 cannot be worst-case-cost measures with a forced answer. There are two ways out, and they give the same measure up to a factor of two: charge the expected number of queries, or keep worst-case cost and allow the answer with probability 1/2 . Markov truncation at twice the expected cost converts the first into the second; repeating until an answer appears converts the second into the first.
